comparison: Perfect agreement on DNA length-dependent binding kinetics (C2, C17-C20, C31). Both evaluations find these claims well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes the linear relationship (R²=0.99) and on-rate limited affinity, while peer reviewers describe the approach as 'extremely elegant' and foundational to understanding target search mechanism.

Disagreement on binding lifetime measurements (C22-C29). OpenEval finds claims well-supported by TIRF data, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning biological relevance of long in vitro binding lifetimes and whether stable DNA association may impede nucleosome binding (comment 9).

Strong agreement on 1D diffusion demonstration (C32-C36, C74). Both identify this as a novel, fundamentally important finding. OpenEval emphasizes the quality of kymograph and MSD analysis data, while peer reviewers explicitly state this is 'the first conclusive demonstration' with implications for other remodelers.

Partial disagreement on ATP enhancement of diffusion (C3, C37-C45). OpenEval finds claims well-supported by comparative data (ATP vs ATPγS vs ADP), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, finding the effect 'intriguing' but requesting additional mechanistic insight to distinguish direct vs allosteric effects (comment 1).

Partial disagreement on Swc2 DBD diffusion (C6, C46-C48). OpenEval finds the 40-fold difference appropriately attributed to size, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting additional experiments to test the 'monkey bar' mechanism with competitor DNA (comments 1, 5).

Agreement on mixed sliding/hopping model (C49-C59). Both find the mechanistic characterization supported by salt-dependence and theoretical comparisons. OpenEval emphasizes multiple lines of evidence, while peer reviewers accept the data but suggest additional competitor DNA experiments to further test hopping hypothesis (comment 5).

Agreement on roadblock experiments (C5, C60-C63). Both find the dCas9 experiments well-designed and supportive of the sliding mechanism. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate quantification and consistency with literature, while peer reviewers raise no concerns about these data.

Disagreement on nucleosome array experiments (C64-C73). OpenEval finds confined diffusion well-demonstrated with appropriate MSD analysis and reasonable confinement length, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting more detailed description and experiments with labeled nucleosomes for 'more confident conclusions' (comment 2).

Agreement on functional validation (C83-C84). Both accept the quality control experiments (glycerol gradient, EMSA) as adequate. OpenEval notes minor limitation of unstated Cy3-Swc7 data, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these technical controls without concern.

Disagreement on biological significance (C74, C75, C82). OpenEval finds scanning time calculation appropriately derived from diffusion data, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether biophysical properties are 'required for correct targeting activity in vivo' and noting the study doesn't establish rate-limiting effects (comments 6, 7).

Disagreement on genomic context interpretation (C78). OpenEval finds NDR context well-established from prior studies, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting 1D diffusion 'does not explain why H2AZ is incorporated into +1 nucleosomes to a greater extent than -1 nucleosomes' and suggesting comparative experiments (comments 4, 10).

Disagreement on sequence-dependence consideration (C88). OpenEval finds citation to prior work on sequence effects appropriate, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, specifically requesting analysis of diffusion coefficients as a function of substrate position to assess AT-content effects (comment 3).

OpenEval evaluates biological context and SWR1 characterization claims (C1, C7-C13) as well-supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/context claims.

OpenEval evaluates claim about LacI diffusion mechanisms (C92) as appropriately supported by citation to prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific literature reference.
